title: Lab & Facilities
text:
The GHYAN Laboratory is equipped with state-of-the-art facilities for sample preparation, characterization, and high-frequency quantum measurements.


  
  
    
    
      Thin Film Deposition
      Capabilities for growing high-quality magnetic and topological thin films with atomic precision.
    
  

  
  
    
    
      Magneto-Optic Kerr Effect
      Custom setup for studying surface magnetization and ultrafast domain dynamics.
    
  

  
  
    
    
      Terahertz Spectroscopy
      Time-domain systems for high-frequency spintronic emission and broad-band characterization.
    
  



Central Research Facilities


Our lab maintains active collaborations with the Central Research Facility at IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, granting our researchers access to advanced structural characterization tools including High-Resolution TEM, FESEM, XRD, and XPS.

title: Research
text:
The Gupta Laboratory for Hybrid Quantum Systems & Spintronics (GHYAN) explores the intersection of fundamental quantum physics and next-generation device applications, focusing on spin and orbital angular momentum in thin films, 2D heterostructures, and nanodevices.

Research Areas


Core experimental thrust areas investigating quantum angular momentum, ultrafast dynamics, and device physics




Magnetism & Spintronics
We study the fundamental magnetic properties of novel materials and how electron spin can be utilized for energy-efficient memory and logic devices. By understanding spin transport, spin-orbit torque (SOT), and magnetization dynamics, we aim to design next-generation magnetic RAM (SOT-MRAM) and spin-logic architectures that drastically reduce standby and switching power consumption.







Orbitronics
Beyond the spin degree of freedom, orbital angular momentum offers an exciting, energy-efficient dimension for information processing. We investigate orbitally-driven transport phenomena, including the orbital Hall effect (OHE) and orbital Rashba-Edelstein effect, in light metals (such as vanadium and titanium) and transition metal oxides, unlocking pathways for high-efficiency torque generation without relying on heavy or scarce elements.







Terahertz Spintronics
Exploring the generation, manipulation, and detection of terahertz (THz) radiation using ultrafast spintronic heterostructures. By exploiting inverse spin Hall effects, anomalous Hall phenomena, and novel full Heusler compounds (such as Co₂FeAl), we develop ultra-broadband, low-cost spintronic THz emitters (STEs) and terahertz spin Hall nano-oscillators for high-speed wireless communication, radar, and non-destructive spectroscopic imaging.







Ultrafast Phenomena
Using ultrafast femtosecond optical and X-ray techniques to probe non-equilibrium spin and magnetization dynamics on sub-picosecond timescales. We investigate how magnetic systems respond to intense femtosecond laser excitation, revealing the fundamental microscopic physics of superdiffusive spin currents, optical demagnetization, and the fundamental speed limits of magnetic state manipulation.











Research Grants and Funding


External and institutional sponsored research projects supporting our experimental investigations and laboratory infrastructure




  
  
    
      
        T-SHNO: Terahertz Spin Hall Nano Oscillator
        
          Swedish Research Council (Vetenskapsrådet - VR) • Project ID: 2023-06605
        
      
      Funded Project
    
    
      Principal Investigator: Dr. Rahul Gupta
      Funding Agency: Vetenskapsrådet (VR), Sweden
      Domain: Terahertz Spintronics & Nano-Devices
      Timeline: 2024 – Present
    
    
      This project focuses on the design, nanofabrication, and experimental demonstration of terahertz spin Hall nano-oscillators (T-SHNOs). The research explores spin-transfer and spin-orbit torques to drive high-frequency magnetic oscillations in nanoscale metallic heterostructures, targeting ultra-broadband coherent emission and synchronization phenomena in the sub-THz and THz spectral regimes.

title: Research
text:
Magnetism & Spintronics
We study the fundamental magnetic properties of novel materials and how electron spin can be utilized for energy-efficient memory and logic devices. By understanding spin transport and dynamics, we aim to design next-generation magnetic RAM and spin-logic architectures that drastically reduce power consumption.

title: Research
text:
Orbitronics
Beyond spin, orbital angular momentum offers a new degree of freedom for information processing. We are pioneering research into orbitally-driven transport phenomena in light metals and transition metal oxides, unlocking pathways for devices that do not rely on heavy spin-orbit coupling.

title: Research
text:
Terahertz Spintronics
Exploring the generation and manipulation of terahertz (THz) radiation using spintronic emitters. These ultra-broadband, low-cost THz sources have immense potential for high-speed communication, imaging, and sensing applications.

title: Research
text:
Ultrafast Phenomena
Using ultrafast optical techniques to understand spin and magnetization dynamics at the femtosecond timescale. We investigate how magnetic systems respond to intense femtosecond laser pulses, revealing the fundamental speed limits of magnetic switching.
